questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जब अंशों/शेयरों का हरण (forfeit) किया जाता है, तो अंश/शेयर पूँजी खाते के नाम में माँगी गई राशि तथा जमा में (i) सम्बन्धित अदत्त याचना खाता अर्थात् अदत्त याचना तथा (ii) अंश/शेयर हरण (forfeit) खाते में अंशों/शेयरों पर पहले से ही प्राप्त राशि होती है ।
कारण (R) : जब अंशों/शेयरों का हरण (forfeit) किया जाता है, तब केवल प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम से सम्बन्धित प्रविष्टियों को छोड़कर अंश/शेयर हरण (forfeit) खाते से सम्बन्धित सभी प्रविष्टियों को जिनका लेखा, लेखांकन पुस्तकों में कर दिया गया है, उलट दिया जाता है ।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): When the shares are forfeited, share capital account is debited with the amount called up and credited to (i) respective unpaid calls account i.e., calls in arrears and (ii) share forfeiture account with the amount already received on shares.
Reason (R): When the shares are forfeited, all entries relating to the shares forfeited, except those relating to securities premium, already recorded in accounting records must be reversed.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है ।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) ग़लत है ।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) incorrect.

questions.solution: Option A is correct because the assertion accurately describes the accounting entry passed during the forfeiture of shares, where the share capital is reduced by debiting it and the unpaid and received amounts are credited. The reason gives the precise logical justification for this accounting treatment, explaining that forfeiture fundamentally involves reversing the capital entries that were originally recorded, effectively cancelling the shares.

Applications were received for 48,000 shares and allotment was made to all the applicants. The amount received on application will be:
questions.solution: Option A is correct because the company received applications for forty-eight thousand equity shares from the public. Since the entire face value and the substantial premium were bundled together making the issue price one hundred and ten rupees per share payable entirely on application, the total application money received equals forty-eight thousand shares multiplied by one hundred and ten, which amounts to fifty-two lakh eighty thousand rupees.

questions.text_english:
Lexa Ltd. issued 50,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 2 per share. The amount was payable as follows:
On application and allotment ₹ 7 per share (including premium)
On first and final call Balance
The issue was fully subscribed. All the money was duly received except the first and final call on 1,000 equity shares. These shares were forfeited. On forfeiture of these shares Calls in Arrears Account will be :
questions.solution: Option C is correct because the balance due on the first and final call is calculated by subtracting the capital portion of the application and allotment money from the face value of the share. Upon default by a shareholder holding one thousand shares, the calls in arrears account is originally debited by five thousand rupees. When these shares are finally forfeited, the calls in arrears account must be closed by crediting it with five thousand rupees.

questions.text_english: The debentures which do not carry a specific rate of interest are called:
questions.solution: Option A is correct because zero coupon rate debentures are fundamentally designed such that they do not bear any explicit or specific rate of interest. Instead, they are typically issued to investors at a significant discount to their face value and are later redeemed at par, with the difference serving as the implicit interest yield for the investor.

Tara's new share becomes three-fifths minus three-tenths, equating to three-tenths or nine-thirtieths. Ojas acquires two-fifteenths plus three-tenths, which aggregates to thirteen-thirtieths. The new ratio therefore becomes eight is to nine is to thirteen.

sub_questions.text_english: Shrikant and Ajay were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3. sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct because the total drawings made by Shrikant during the year amount to forty thousand rupees. questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : 'स्थायी पूँजी विधि' में साझेदारों के चालू खाते बनाए जाते हैं जो नाम शेष भी दर्शा सकते हैं और जमा शेष भी ।
कारण (R) : 'स्थायी पूँजी विधि' में सभी मदों जैसे लाभ या हानि का भाग, पूँजी पर ब्याज, आहरण, आहरण पर ब्याज आदि का लेखा साझेदारों के पूँजी खातों में किया जाता है ।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Partners' current accounts maintained under 'Fixed Capital Method' may show a debit or a credit balance.
Reason (R): In the 'Fixed Capital Method', all items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings etc. are recorded in the partners' capital accounts.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है ।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही नहीं है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों ग़लत हैं ।

options_english.A: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is not correct.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are not correct.

questions.solution: Option C is correct because the assertion is an accurate statement; partners' current accounts can indeed have either a debit or credit balance depending on the accumulated drawings and losses versus profits. However, the reason is entirely incorrect because under the Fixed Capital Method, items like interest on capital, drawings, and share of profits are recorded exclusively in the partners' current accounts, not their capital accounts.

questions.text_english: Seema and Laksh were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1. Their capitals were ₹ 2,00,000 and ₹ 1,80,000 respectively. They admitted Aadi as a new partner on 1st April, 2023 for 1/5th share in future profits. Aadi brought ₹ 1,50,000 as his share of capital. The goodwill of the firm on Aadi's admission will be :
questions.solution: Option B is correct because the total capitalized value of the firm based on Aadi's capital is calculated as one lakh fifty thousand multiplied by five, which equals seven lakh fifty thousand rupees. The actual total capital of all partners combined is two lakh plus one lakh eighty thousand plus one lakh fifty thousand, amounting to five lakh thirty thousand rupees. The hidden goodwill is the difference between the total capitalized value and the actual total capital, which is two lakh twenty thousand rupees.

questions.text: गीता तथा हरी एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । कृष को फर्म के लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया जो उसने गीता तथा हरी से 2:3 के अनुपात में अधिग्रहित किया । कृष अपनी पूँजी के भाग के रूप में ₹ 1,00,000 तथा ख्याति प्रीमियम के रूप में ₹ 50,000 नगद लाया। गीता तथा हरी का त्याग अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Geeta and Hari were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Krish was admitted as a new partner for 1/5th share in profits of the firm which he acquired from Geeta and Hari in the ratio of 2:3. Krish brought ₹ 1,00,000 as his share of capital and ₹ 50,000 as premium for goodwill in cash. The sacrificing ratio of Geeta and Hari will be:
questions.solution: Option C is correct because the new partner Krish acquires his designated share of profit entirely from Geeta and Hari precisely in the ratio of two is to three as explicitly stated in the problem. The proportion in which the old partners surrender their share to the new partner represents their sacrificing ratio, making it exactly two is to three.

questions.text:
संगीत, अंजू तथा शिवा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि का विभाजन 3:4:5 के अनुपात में करते थे । 31 जुलाई, 2023 को संगीत की मृत्यु हो गई । मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभों में संगीत के भाग की गणना विक्रय के आधार पर की जाएगी। 2022 - 2023 वर्ष के दौरान विक्रय की राशि ₹ 40,00,000 थी तथा 1 अप्रैल, 2023 से 31 जुलाई, 2023 तक विक्रय ₹ 10,00,000 था । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का लाभ ₹ 4,00,000 था ।
मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में संगीत के भाग की गणना कीजिए तथा फर्म की पुस्तकों में इसके लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टि कीजिए। अपने कार्य को स्पष्टता से दर्शाइए ।
questions.text_english:
Sangeet, Anju and Shiva were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:4:5. Sangeet died on 31st July, 2023. Sangeet's share in the profits of the firm till the date of death was to be calculated on the basis of sales. Sales during the year 2022-23 were ₹ 40,00,000 and sales from 1st April, 2023 to 31st July, 2023 were ₹ 10,00,000. The profit for the year ended 31st March, 2023 was ₹ 4,00,000.
Calculate Sangeet's share of profit up to the date of death and pass the necessary journal entry for the same in the books of the firm. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Calculate Profit percentage on sales for the previous year
Apply the percentage to the current year's sales up to the date of death to find total firm profit
Calculate Sangeet's specific share from the total firm profit
Pass the journal entry debiting P&L Suspense A/c and crediting Sangeet's Capital A/c

questions.solution: To calculate Sangeet's share of profit, we first determine the profit percentage based on the previous year's figures. A profit of four lakh rupees on sales of forty lakh rupees indicates a profit margin of ten percent. Applying this ten percent margin to the current year's sales of ten lakh rupees gives an estimated total profit of one lakh rupees for the firm up to the date of death. Sangeet's share in the profit is three-twelfths of this amount, which is exactly twenty-five thousand rupees. The corresponding journal entry requires debiting the Profit and Loss Suspense Account with twenty-five thousand rupees and crediting Sangeet's Capital Account with twenty-five thousand rupees.

questions.text: सुमन और धवन की फर्म का पिछले पाँच वर्षों का औसत लाभ ₹ 6,00,000 था । इसी प्रकार के व्यवसाय में प्रतिफल की सामान्य दर 10% है। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन अधिलाभ की पूँजीकरण विधि द्वारा ₹ 40,00,000 किया गया। फर्म द्वारा विनियोजित पूँजी की राशि की गणना कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: The average profit for last five years of a firm of Suman and Dhawan was ₹ 6,00,000. The normal rate of return in a similar business is 10%. Goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹ 40,00,000 calculated by capitalisation of super profit. Find out the amount of capital employed by the firm.

key_points: State formula: Goodwill = Super Profit * (100 / NRR)
Calculate Super Profit using the Goodwill value
Calculate Normal Profit by subtracting Super Profit from Average Profit
Calculate Capital Employed using the Normal Profit and NRR

questions.solution: First, we must work backwards from the goodwill valuation. Under the capitalization of super profit method, Goodwill equals Super Profit multiplied by one hundred divided by the normal rate of return. Given a goodwill of forty lakh rupees and a normal rate of return of ten percent, the Super Profit computes to exactly four lakh rupees. Since Super Profit is the excess of Average Profit over Normal Profit, we subtract the four lakh rupees from the given average profit of six lakh rupees to find the Normal Profit, which is two lakh rupees. Finally, the Capital Employed is calculated by capitalizing the Normal Profit; dividing two lakh rupees by the ten percent return rate reveals that the capital employed by the firm is exactly twenty lakh rupees.

sub_questions.text_english: Sumi Ltd. acquired assets of ₹ 8,00,000 and took over sundry creditors of ₹ 2,00,000 from Pandora Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹ 9,00,000. The payment was made by issuing a cheque of ₹ 4,60,000 and remaining by issue of 9% Debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 10%. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Sumi Ltd.

key_points: Record asset acquisition and identify Goodwill
Record partial payment by Bank
Record issue of debentures at a premium for the remaining balance

sub_questions.solution:
In the books of Sumi Ltd., the first journal entry records the acquisition of assets and liabilities. Sundry Assets Account is debited with eight lakh rupees. Since the net assets acquired amount to six lakh rupees but the purchase consideration is nine lakh rupees, the difference of three lakh rupees represents Goodwill, so the Goodwill Account is debited with three lakh rupees. The Sundry Creditors Account is credited with two lakh rupees and Pandora Ltd. Account is credited with nine lakh rupees. 
For the settlement, Pandora Ltd. Account is debited with nine lakh rupees. The Bank Account is credited with four lakh sixty thousand rupees for the cheque payment. The remaining balance of four lakh forty thousand rupees is discharged by issuing debentures at a ten percent premium. Dividing four lakh forty thousand by the issue price of one hundred and ten rupees gives four thousand debentures. Thus, the 9% Debentures Account is credited with four lakh rupees and the Securities Premium Account is credited with forty thousand rupees.

sub_questions.text: गुंडोला लिमिटेड ने एके लिमिटेड से ₹ 9,00,000 की परिसम्पत्तियों तथा ₹ 3,00,000 की देयताओं का अधिग्रहण ₹ 14,00,000 के सहमत क्रय मूल्य पर किया । भुगतान ₹ 5,00,000 के एक बैंक ड्राफ्ट द्वारा तथा शेष के लिए 10% की छूट पर 8% ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन द्वारा किया गया । उपर्युक्त लेनदेन के लिए गुंडोला लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Gundola Ltd. took over assets of ₹ 9,00,000 and liabilities of ₹ 3,00,000 from AK Ltd. for an agreed purchase consideration of ₹ 14,00,000. The payment was made through a bank draft of ₹ 5,00,000 and the remaining by issue of 8% Debentures at a discount of 10%. Record necessary journal entries in the books of Gundola Ltd. for the above transactions.

key_points: Record asset acquisition and identify Goodwill
Record partial payment by Bank Draft
Record issue of debentures at a discount for the remaining balance

sub_questions.solution:
In the books of Gundola Ltd., the initial entry documents the business acquisition. The Sundry Assets Account is debited with nine lakh rupees. The net worth of the business acquired is six lakh rupees, but the purchase consideration is agreed at fourteen lakh rupees. The eight lakh rupees excess is recognised as Goodwill, so the Goodwill Account is debited with eight lakh rupees. Consequently, the Sundry Liabilities Account is credited with three lakh rupees and AK Ltd. Account is credited with fourteen lakh rupees.
For the payment phase, AK Ltd. is debited with fourteen lakh rupees. The Bank Account is credited with five lakh rupees for the draft payment. To settle the remaining nine lakh rupees, debentures are issued at a ten percent discount. Dividing nine lakh rupees by the issue price of ninety gives ten thousand debentures. Therefore, the Discount on Issue of Debentures Account is debited with one lakh rupees, and the 8% Debentures Account is credited with ten lakh rupees, ensuring the transaction balances accurately.

sub_questions.text: मिशा तथा प्रिशा एक फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। 1 अप्रैल, 2022 को उनके पूँजी खाते क्रमशः ₹ 50,000 तथा ₹ 30,000 के शेष दर्शा रहे थे। वर्ष के दौरान मिशा ने ₹ 12,900, जबकि प्रिशा ने ₹ 9,600 का आहरण किया। उन्हें 10% वार्षिक दर से पूँजी पर ब्याज अनुमत किया गया था। मिशा के आहरण पर ₹ 660 का ब्याज तथा प्रिशा के आहरण पर ₹ 540 का ब्याज प्रभारित किया गया । 1 अगस्त, 2022 को प्रिशा ने फर्म को ₹ 20,000 का ऋण दिया । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 22,600 था । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का लाभ-हानि विनियोग खाता तैयार कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Misha and Prisha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. On 1st April, 2022, their capital accounts showed balances of ₹ 50,000 and ₹ 30,000 respectively. During the year, Misha withdrew ₹ 12,900 while Prisha withdrew ₹ 9,600. They were allowed interest on capital @ 10% p.a. Interest on drawings of ₹ 660 was charged on Misha's drawings and ₹ 540 on Prisha's drawings. Prisha had advanced a loan of ₹ 20,000 to the firm on 1st August, 2022. The net profit for the year ended 31st March, 2023 amounted to ₹ 22,600. Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year ended 31st March, 2023.

key_points: Calculate Interest on Partner's Loan and deduct from Net Profit
Calculate Interest on Capital
Add Interest on Drawings to distributable profit pool
Distribute final Divisible Profit in agreed ratio

sub_questions.solution:
To prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, we first adjust the given net profit for Prisha's interest on loan, as it is a strict charge against profit. The loan of twenty thousand rupees attracts interest at a statutory rate of six percent per annum for exactly eight months, amounting to eight hundred rupees. Subtracting this from the initial profit leaves an adjusted net profit of twenty-one thousand eight hundred rupees, which is credited to the Appropriation Account. We then add the total interest on drawings of one thousand two hundred rupees to the credit side. 
On the debit side, interest on capital is provided at ten percent. Misha receives five thousand rupees and Prisha receives three thousand rupees, totalling eight thousand rupees. The remaining divisible profit is then ascertained by subtracting the eight thousand rupees from the total credit pool of twenty-three thousand rupees, leaving exactly fifteen thousand rupees. This profit is distributed in their mutually agreed ratio of three is to two, resulting in nine thousand rupees being credited to Misha's capital account and six thousand rupees to Prisha's capital account.

sub_questions.text: 31 मार्च, 2023 को आहरण व शुद्ध लाभ के सम्बन्ध में सभी आवश्यक समायोजन करने के पश्चात् राघव तथा दिया की पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 4,00,000 तथा ₹ 3,00,000 थी । बाद में यह ज्ञात हुआ कि 10% वार्षिक दर से पूँजी पर ब्याज नहीं दिया गया । 31 मार्च, 2023 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 1,00,000 था । 31 मार्च, 2023 वर्ष के दौरान, राघव के आहरण प्रत्येक माह के आरम्भ में ₹ 2,000, जबकि दिया के आहरण प्रत्येक तिमाही के आरम्भ में ₹ 3,000 थे । आवश्यक समायोजन प्रविष्टि कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: On 31st March, 2023, the capitals of Raghav and Diya stood at ₹ 4,00,000 and ₹ 3,00,000 respectively, after the necessary adjustment in respect of drawings and net profit. Subsequently, it was discovered that interest on capital @ 10% p.a had been omitted. The Net Profit for the year ended 31st March, 2023 amounted to ₹ 1,00,000. During the year ended 31st March, 2023, Raghav's drawings were ₹ 2,000 drawn at the beginning of each month, while Diya's drawings were ₹ 3,000 drawn at the beginning of each quarter. Pass the necessary adjustment entry.

key_points: Calculate Opening Capitals by reversing profit and drawings
Compute omitted Interest on Capital based on opening capital
Calculate net effect of the omission and share of loss caused by it
Pass the final single rectifying adjustment entry

sub_questions.solution:
First, the opening capital of both partners must be determined by working backward from their closing balances. Assuming an equal profit sharing ratio since no specific ratio is provided, the profit of one lakh rupees is equally reversed, deducting fifty thousand rupees from each partner's account. Raghav's total drawings of twenty-four thousand rupees and Diya's total drawings of twelve thousand rupees are then added back. This yields opening capital balances of three lakh seventy-four thousand rupees for Raghav and two lakh sixty-two thousand rupees for Diya. 
The omitted interest on capital at ten percent calculates to thirty-seven thousand four hundred rupees for Raghav and twenty-six thousand two hundred rupees for Diya, creating a total firm expense of sixty-three thousand six hundred rupees. This expense constitutes a loss to be borne equally by the partners, meaning each partner is debited with thirty-one thousand eight hundred rupees. Analysing the net effect, Raghav receives a net credit of five thousand six hundred rupees, whilst Diya suffers a net debit of five thousand six hundred rupees. The single rectifying journal entry requires debiting Diya's Capital Account with five thousand six hundred rupees and crediting Raghav's Capital Account with the corresponding five thousand six hundred rupees.

श्री गंगा लिमिटेड ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के समता अंशों/शेयरों में विभक्त ₹ 7,00,000 की अधिकृत पूँजी के साथ पंजीकृत थी। इसने जनता को अभिदान के लिए 50,000 समता अंश/शेयर प्रस्तुत किए । राशि का भुगतान निम्न प्रकार से देय था :
आवेदन पर : ₹ 4 प्रति अंश/शेयर
आबंटन पर : ₹ 4 प्रति अंश/शेयर
प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना पर : शेष
निर्गम पूर्ण रूप से अभिदत्त हुआ । 4,000 समता अंशों/शेयरों पर प्रथम एवं अंतिम याचना राशि के अतिरिक्त सभी राशियाँ विधिवत् प्राप्त हो गईं । कम्पनी अधिनियम, 2013 की अनुसूची III, भाग I के अनुसार कम्पनी के स्थिति विवरण में अंश/शेयर पूँजी को दर्शाइए। इसी के लिए 'खातों के नोट्स' भी तैयार कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Shri Ganga Ltd. was registered with an authorised capital of ₹ 7,00,000 divided into equity shares of ₹ 10 each. It offered to the public for subscription 50,000 equity shares. The amount was payable as follows:
On application : ₹ 4 per share
On allotment : ₹ 4 per share
On first and final call : Balance
The issue was fully subscribed. All the amounts were duly received except the first and final call money on 4,000 equity shares. Show the Share Capital in the Balance Sheet of the company as per Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act, 2013. Also prepare 'Notes to Accounts' for the same.

key_points: Present Share Capital in the main Balance Sheet format
Detail Authorised, Issued, and Subscribed Capital in Notes to Accounts
Distinguish between fully paid up and not fully paid up subscribed capital
Correctly deduct Calls in Arrears to show the final amount

questions.solution:
To present the Share Capital correctly in the Balance Sheet of Shri Ganga Ltd. as per Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act, 2013, an amount of four lakh ninety-two thousand rupees is shown under the main heading 'Equity and Liabilities', sub-heading 'Shareholders' Funds', specifically against the line item 'Share Capital'.
In the Notes to Accounts, the details are systematically expanded. First, the Authorised Capital is declared as seventy thousand equity shares of ten rupees each, totalling seven lakh rupees. Second, the Issued Capital is noted as fifty thousand equity shares of ten rupees each, amounting to five lakh rupees. Third, the Subscribed Capital is distinctly categorised. Under the sub-classification 'Subscribed and fully paid-up', forty-six thousand equity shares of ten rupees each are listed, yielding four lakh sixty thousand rupees. Under the sub-classification 'Subscribed but not fully paid-up', the remaining four thousand shares are listed. The total called-up value on these shares is forty thousand rupees. From this, the calls in arrears regarding the final call of two rupees per share on four thousand shares, which strictly equals eight thousand rupees, is deducted. This leaves a balance of thirty-two thousand rupees for this category. Adding both subscribed categories together results in the final share capital figure of four lakh ninety-two thousand rupees that is prominently transferred to the main Balance Sheet.

फ्रैंक, जॉर्ज तथा हेमन्त एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभों का विभाजन करते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2023 से उन्होंने लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात को 2:5:3 में परिवर्तित करने का निर्णय लिया । 31 मार्च, 2023 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न प्रकार था :
31 मार्च, 2023 को फ्रैंक, जॉर्ज तथा हेमन्त का स्थिति विवरण
| देयताएँ | राशि (₹) | परिसम्पत्तियाँ | राशि (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| पूँजी : | | भूमि | 5,00,000 |
| फ्रैंक | 4,00,000 | भवन | 3,00,000 |
| जॉर्ज | 3,00,000 | मशीनरी | 2,00,000 |
| हेमन्त | 2,00,000 | स्टॉक | 1,50,000 |
| लेनदार | 5,00,000 | देनदार | 2,50,000 |
| कर्मचारी भविष्य निधि | 1,00,000 | रोकड़ | 3,00,000 |
| सामान्य संचय | 2,00,000 | | |

यह निर्णय लिया गया कि :
(i) भूमि के मूल्य में वृद्धि हुई और इसे ₹ 6,50,000 तक लाया जाए ।
(ii) फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 2,00,000 किया गया। ख्याति को फर्म की पुस्तकों में नहीं दर्शाया जाएगा ।
फर्म की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Frank, George and Hemant were partners in a firm sharing profits in the ratio of 5:3:2. They decided to change their profit sharing ratio to 2:5:3 with effect from 1st April, 2023. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2023 was as follows:
Balance Sheet of Frank, George and Hemant as at 31st March, 2023
| Liabilities | Amount (₹) | Assets | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capitals: | | Land | 5,00,000 |
| Frank | 4,00,000 | Building | 3,00,000 |
| George | 3,00,000 | Machinery | 2,00,000 |
| Hemant | 2,00,000 | Stock | 1,50,000 |
| Creditors | 5,00,000 | Debtors | 2,50,000 |
| Employees' Provident Fund | 1,00,000 | Cash | 3,00,000 |
| General Reserve | 2,00,000 | | |
| Total | 17,00,000 | Total | 17,00,000 |

It was decided that:
(i) The value of land having appreciated be brought up to ₹ 6,50,000.
(ii) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 2,00,000. Goodwill was not to appear in the books of the firm.
Pass the necessary journal entries in the books of the firm.

key_points: Record the revaluation of land and distribute the revaluation profit to partners
Distribute accumulated General Reserve in the old profit sharing ratio
Calculate the sacrificing and gaining ratios for all partners
Pass the adjusting journal entry for goodwill through capital accounts

questions.solution:
To give effect to the agreed changes, several journal entries must be recorded in the firm's books. First, the appreciation in the value of the land is documented by debiting the Land Account with one lakh fifty thousand rupees and crediting the Revaluation Account with the corresponding amount. This creates a revaluation profit of one lakh fifty thousand rupees, which is subsequently distributed among the partners. The Revaluation Account is therefore debited, and the Capital Accounts of Frank, George, and Hemant are credited with seventy-five thousand, forty-five thousand, and thirty thousand rupees respectively, adhering to their old five is to three is to two ratio. 
Secondly, the accumulated General Reserve must be distributed. The General Reserve Account is debited entirely with two lakh rupees, and the Capital Accounts of Frank, George, and Hemant are similarly credited with one lakh, sixty thousand, and forty thousand rupees respectively. Note that the Employees' Provident Fund is a statutory liability and is strictly not distributed.
Finally, the adjustment for goodwill is required. Frank's old share was five-tenths and his new share is two-tenths, resulting in a sacrifice of three-tenths. George gains two-tenths, and Hemant gains one-tenth. The total goodwill is valued at two lakh rupees. Consequently, George's Capital Account is debited with forty thousand rupees, and Hemant's Capital Account is debited with twenty thousand rupees, while Frank's Capital Account is credited with sixty thousand rupees to precisely compensate him for his sacrifice without opening a distinct Goodwill Account.
questions.topic: Revaluation of Assets and Adjustment of Reserves and Goodwill

उपर्युक्त तिथि को निम्नलिखित शर्तों पर फर्म का विघटन हो गया :
(i) स्थायी परिसम्पत्तियों की वसूली पुस्तक मूल्य से 15% कम पर हुई ।
(ii) व्यापारिक प्राप्य पुस्तक मूल्य पर वसूल हुए ।
(iii) निवेशों को फ्लोरा ने ₹ 6,00,000 में ले लिया ।

questions.text_english:
David, Eden and Flora were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. On 31st March, 2023, their Balance Sheet was as follows:
Balance Sheet of David, Eden and Flora as at 31st March, 2023
| Liabilities | Amount (₹) | Assets | Amount (₹) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capital: | | Fixed Assets | 10,00,000 |
| David | 6,00,000 | Investments | 5,00,000 |
| Eden | 6,00,000 | Stock | 3,00,000 |
| Flora | 6,00,000 | Bills Receivable | 2,00,000 |
| General Reserve | 3,00,000 | Cash at Bank | 2,00,000 |
| Bills Payable | 1,00,000 | | |
| Total | 22,00,000 | Total | 22,00,000 |

On the above date, the firm was dissolved on the following terms:
(i) Fixed Assets were realised at 15% less than the book value.
(ii) Trade Receivables were realised at book value.
(iii) Investments were taken over by Flora at ₹ 6,00,000.
(iv) David took over 50% of the stock at ₹ 1,80,000. The remaining stock was taken over by Eden at ₹ 95,000.
(v) Expenses of realisation amounted to ₹ 25,000 and were paid by Flora.
Prepare Realisation Account.

key_points: Transfer all non-cash assets to the debit side of Realisation Account
Transfer external liabilities to the credit side of Realisation Account
Record asset realisations and partner takeovers on the credit side
Record payment of liabilities and expenses on the debit side
Calculate final profit or loss and distribute among partners

questions.solution:
The Realisation Account is prepared by initially transferring all existing assets, barring cash at bank, to the debit side. This includes Fixed Assets at ten lakh, Investments at five lakh, Stock at three lakh, and Bills Receivable at two lakh rupees, yielding a total debit of twenty lakh rupees. Conversely, the external liability, which consists exclusively of Bills Payable amounting to one lakh rupees, is transferred to the credit side.
For the asset realisations recorded on the credit side, Flora's Capital Account is debited with six lakh rupees for taking over the investments. David's Capital Account is debited with one lakh eighty thousand rupees for half the stock, and Eden's Capital Account is debited with ninety-five thousand rupees for the remaining stock. The Bank Account is credited with a total of ten lakh fifty thousand rupees, which represents eight lakh fifty thousand from fixed assets (fifteen percent less than ten lakh) and two lakh from bills receivable (realised at book value).
On the debit side, payments include the full settlement of Bills Payable for one lakh rupees through the Bank Account, as no alternative instructions were provided. The realisation expenses of twenty-five thousand rupees paid by Flora are recorded by crediting Flora's Capital Account. Summing both sides, the credit side aggregates to twenty lakh twenty-five thousand rupees, while the debit items total twenty-one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees. This reveals a net realisation loss of one lakh rupees. This loss is distributed in their profit-sharing ratio of two is to two is to one, resulting in David's and Eden's capital accounts each being debited with forty thousand rupees, and Flora's capital account being debited with twenty thousand rupees.

questions.text_english:
On 1st April, 2022, Centafit Ltd. issued 2,000, 7% Debentures of ₹ 500 each at a premium of 10%, redeemable at a premium of 10% after five years. The company had a balance of ₹ 1,75,000 in 'Securities Premium Account' before the issue.
(a) Pass journal entries for issue of debentures and for writing off Loss on Issue of Debentures' utilising Securities Premium Account at the end of the first year itself.
(b) Prepare 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account' for the year ended 31st March, 2023.

sub_questions.text: ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन तथा 'ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर हानि' को प्रथम वर्ष में ही प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते का उपयोग करते हुए अपलिखित करने के लिए रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Pass journal entries for issue of debentures and for writing off Loss on Issue of Debentures' utilising Securities Premium Account at the end of the first year itself.

key_points: Record receipt of application money including issue premium
Transfer application money to Debentures Account, record premium on issue and provide for premium on redemption
Write off the Loss on Issue of Debentures fully against the total available Securities Premium balance

sub_questions.solution:
In the journal of Centafit Ltd., the first entry on April 1, 2022, records the receipt of application money. The Bank Account is debited and the Debenture Application and Allotment Account is credited with eleven lakh rupees, which accurately reflects the face value of ten lakh rupees plus the ten percent issue premium of one lakh rupees. 
The second entry transfers these funds and sets up the redemption liability. The Debenture Application and Allotment Account is debited with eleven lakh rupees. Simultaneously, the Loss on Issue of Debentures Account is debited with one lakh rupees, representing the future ten percent premium payable upon redemption on the base of ten lakh. The 7% Debentures Account is credited with the nominal face value of ten lakh rupees. The Securities Premium Account is credited with one lakh rupees representing the issue premium, and the Premium on Redemption of Debentures Account is credited with one lakh rupees, establishing the liability.
At the financial year-end on March 31, 2023, the loss must be written off. The company possesses an adequate Securities Premium balance (one lakh seventy-five thousand pre-existing plus one lakh from the current issue). The Securities Premium Account is debited with one lakh rupees, and the Loss on Issue of Debentures Account is credited with the identical amount to entirely write it off.

Pass necessary journal entries for forfeiture and reissue of shares in the following cases:
(i) Neon Ltd. forfeited 2,000 shares of ₹ 10 each issued at a premium of ₹ 2 per share for non-payment of allotment money of ₹ 5 per share (including premium). The first and final call of ₹ 2 per share was not yet made. Out of these, 1,500 shares were reissued at ₹ 7 per share, ₹ 8 paid up.
(ii) Mamta Ltd. forfeited 3,000 shares of ₹ 10 each on which the first call of ₹ 3 per share was not received. The second and final call of ₹ 1 per share was not yet called. Out of these, 2,000 shares were reissued at ₹ 9 per share, ₹ 9 paid up.

key_points: Neon Ltd: Record forfeiture with called-up capital and unpaid premium
Neon Ltd: Record reissue at a discount and calculate Capital Reserve transfer proportionately
Mamta Ltd: Record forfeiture with correct called-up capital
Mamta Ltd: Record reissue without discount and calculate correct Capital Reserve transfer

sub_questions.solution:
For Neon Ltd., the share capital called up is eight rupees per share since the final call of two rupees was never made. Upon forfeiture, the Share Capital Account is debited with sixteen thousand rupees, and the Securities Premium Account is debited with four thousand rupees because the premium remained unpaid. The Share Forfeiture Account is credited with the received application money of ten thousand rupees, and the Share Allotment Account is credited with the ten thousand rupees unpaid balance. During the reissue of one thousand five hundred shares, the Bank Account is debited with ten thousand five hundred rupees, and the Share Forfeiture Account is debited with one thousand five hundred rupees to cover the discount. The Share Capital Account is credited with twelve thousand rupees. Finally, the proportionate forfeiture balance of seven thousand five hundred rupees minus the reissue discount leaves precisely six thousand rupees to be transferred directly to the Capital Reserve Account. 
For Mamta Ltd., the shares are forfeited after the first call, making the called-up capital nine rupees per share. The Share Capital Account is debited with twenty-seven thousand rupees. The Share First Call Account is credited with nine thousand rupees, and the Share Forfeiture Account is credited with the received sum of eighteen thousand rupees. During the subsequent reissue of two thousand shares as nine rupees paid up for exactly nine rupees per share, the Bank Account is debited with eighteen thousand rupees and the Share Capital Account is credited with eighteen thousand rupees. Since no discount was provided upon this reissue, the entire proportionate forfeited amount for these shares, which strictly equals twelve thousand rupees, is transferred directly to the Capital Reserve Account.

Sarah and Varsha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2023 was as follows:

|---|---|---|---|

| Sarah | 60,000 | Stock | 30,000 |
| Varsha | 50,000 | 1,10,000 | Debtors | 50,000 |
| Workmen's Compensation Fund | 20,000 | Less: Provision for doubtful debts | 5,000 | 45,000 |
| Provident Fund | 1,20,000 | Cash | 25,000 |
| Creditors | 50,000 | | |
| Total | 3,00,000 | Total | 3,00,000 |

On 1st April, 2023, they decided to admit Tasha as a new partner for 1/4th share in the profits of the firm on the following terms:
(i) Tasha brought ₹ 40,000 as her capital and ₹ 20,000 as her share of premium for goodwill.
(ii) Plant and Machinery was valued at ₹ 1,90,000.
(iii) An item of ₹ 20,000, included in creditors, is not likely to be claimed and should be written off.
(iv) Capitals of the partners in the new firm are to be in the new profit sharing ratio on the basis of Tasha's capital, by bringing or paying off cash, as the case may be.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Prepare Revaluation Account capturing depreciation of machinery and write-back of creditors
Calculate new profit sharing ratio and the total capital of the firm based on the incoming partner
Distribute Workmen Compensation Fund and Goodwill premium to old partners
Prepare Capital accounts adjusting surplus/deficit through Cash accounts

sub_questions.solution:
To properly reconstruct the firm's accounts upon Tasha's admission, we first draft the Revaluation Account. On the debit side, Plant and Machinery is reduced by ten thousand rupees. On the credit side, the unclaimed Creditors amount of twenty thousand rupees is documented. This generates a net revaluation profit of ten thousand rupees, which is subsequently distributed in the old ratio of three is to two. Hence, Sarah's capital is credited with six thousand rupees and Varsha's with four thousand rupees.
Next, we address the Partners' Capital Accounts. The opening balances are sixty thousand for Sarah and fifty thousand for Varsha. The Workmen Compensation Fund of twenty thousand rupees, having no associated claims, is entirely transferred to them, crediting twelve thousand to Sarah and eight thousand to Varsha. Tasha introduces a capital of forty thousand rupees alongside a goodwill premium of twenty thousand rupees. Because no alternative sacrificing ratio is provided, the premium is shared in their original ratio, crediting twelve thousand to Sarah and eight thousand to Varsha. After adding the revaluation profit, the adjusted capitals stand at ninety thousand for Sarah and seventy thousand for Varsha.
The final step involves capital realignment based on Tasha's contribution. Given Tasha brings forty thousand for a one-quarter share, the total capital of the newly constituted firm must be one lakh sixty thousand rupees. The new profit-sharing ratio mathematically works out to nine is to six is to five. Consequently, the mandated new capitals are seventy-two thousand for Sarah, forty-eight thousand for Varsha, and forty thousand for Tasha. Comparing adjusted balances with these required balances, Sarah possesses an excess of eighteen thousand rupees, and Varsha an excess of twenty-two thousand rupees. Therefore, these surplus amounts are strictly paid out to them in cash, effectively closing their capital accounts at the required proportional figures.

|---|---|---|---|

Kapil retired from the firm on 31st March, 2023 on the following terms:
(i) Bad Debts amounting to ₹ 5,000 were to be written off.
(ii) Fixed Assets were revalued at ₹ 96,000.
(iii) Stock was undervalued by ₹ 29,000.
(iv) Creditors were paid off.
(v) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 80,000 and Kapil's share of goodwill was to be adjusted in the accounts of Inder and Jonny.
(vi) New profit sharing ratio between Inder and Jonny was 3:2.
Pass the necessary journal entries in the books of the firm on Kapil's retirement.

key_points: Record journal entries for all revaluation items including bad debts, asset depreciation, and stock appreciation
Transfer the net revaluation result to all partners' capital accounts
Distribute the General Reserve among all partners in their old profit-sharing ratio
Record the settlement of creditors
Calculate gaining ratio and adjust the retiring partner's share of goodwill through the continuing partners' capital accounts
Transfer the final balance of the retiring partner to his loan account

sub_questions.solution:
Upon Kapil's retirement, several sequential journal entries must be recorded. Firstly, the revaluation of assets requires adjustment. The Revaluation Account is debited with twenty-nine thousand rupees to account for bad debts of five thousand and a twenty-four thousand decrease in fixed assets, while Debtors and Fixed Assets accounts are correspondingly credited. Simultaneously, the Stock Account is debited with twenty-nine thousand rupees for its prior undervaluation, crediting the Revaluation Account. This exact offsetting results in no net profit or loss on revaluation, therefore requiring no distribution entry for the same.
Next, the accumulated General Reserve of eighty thousand rupees must be distributed. The General Reserve Account is debited entirely, and the capital accounts of Inder, Jonny, and Kapil are credited with forty-five thousand, fifteen thousand, and twenty thousand rupees respectively, adhering to their old nine is to three is to four ratio.
The payment to creditors is documented by debiting the Creditors Account and crediting the Cash or Bank Account with ten thousand rupees.
The critical adjustment involves goodwill. Kapil's four-sixteenths share of the eighty thousand total firm goodwill amounts strictly to twenty thousand rupees. Analysing the change from the old ratio to the new three is to two ratio reveals that Inder's share marginally increased by three-eightieths, whereas Jonny gained seventeen-eightieths. To properly compensate Kapil, Jonny's Capital Account is heavily debited with seventeen thousand rupees, and Inder's Capital Account is debited with three thousand rupees, effectively crediting Kapil's Capital Account with the total twenty thousand rupees based on their respective gains.
Finally, Kapil's total accumulated balance must be settled. His initial capital was sixty thousand rupees, augmented by his reserve share of twenty thousand and his goodwill compensation of twenty thousand, establishing a final balance of one lakh rupees. Without instructions to pay cash, Kapil's Capital Account is debited with one lakh rupees, and Kapil's Loan Account is credited with the identical amount to signify the firm's ongoing liability.

questions.solution: Option B is correct because the debt-equity ratio strictly compares long-term debt to shareholders' equity. The issue of debentures directly increases the long-term debt without affecting the equity, causing the numerator of the ratio to rise, thereby resulting in an overall increase in the debt-equity ratio. Second, 'Stores and Spares' are routinely classified under the major head 'Current Assets' and specifically allocated to the sub-head 'Inventories', as they form an essential part of consumable operating assets.

To calculate the Proprietary Ratio, one must primarily establish the total Shareholders' Funds and the Total Assets. The Shareholders' Funds consist of the Share Capital amounting to twelve lakh rupees and the Reserves and Surplus of three lakh rupees, summing to fifteen lakh rupees. 
Next, the Total Assets can be reliably determined by aggregating the total of the equity and liabilities side, as both sides of the balance sheet must match. Determine final Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities as an outflow
Identify cash inflows from the issue of share capital and bank loan
Identify cash outflows due to reduction in bank overdraft, interest, and dividend payments
Determine final Net Cash Flow from Financing Activities as an inflow

questions.solution:
To calculate the Cash Flows from Investing Activities, a Plant and Machinery Account must be constructed. The opening balance is three lakh rupees. A machine with a book value of seventy thousand rupees, computed from a cost of eighty-five thousand minus accumulated depreciation of fifteen thousand, is sold for sixty-two thousand rupees, incurring an eight thousand rupee loss. Thus, the account is credited with the sale proceeds of sixty-two thousand, the loss of eight thousand, and the current year depreciation of forty-eight thousand. Subtracting the initial three lakh balance from the total closing side figure of five lakh twenty-eight thousand reveals a balancing figure on the debit side of two lakh twenty-eight thousand rupees, indicating fresh purchases. Additionally, the Goodwill balance increases from eighty thousand to one lakh eighty thousand, denoting a purchase of one lakh rupees. Aggregating the sale proceeds inflow of sixty-two thousand against the heavy outflows of two lakh twenty-eight thousand for machinery and one lakh for goodwill yields a Net Cash Used in Investing Activities amounting to strictly two lakh sixty-six thousand rupees.
Moving to the Cash Flows from Financing Activities, the issue of Equity Share Capital generates a robust cash inflow of five lakh rupees, as it rises from ten lakh to fifteen lakh. The Bank Loan increases by one lakh rupees, adding another inflow. Conversely, there are several distinct outflows. The Bank Overdraft decreases from one lakh twenty thousand to ninety thousand, signaling a repayment of thirty thousand rupees. Furthermore, the mandatory payment of interest on the bank loan consumes sixty thousand rupees, and the dividend disbursement drains another one lakh ten thousand rupees. Netting these amounts together by adding the inflows of six lakh rupees and subtracting the cumulative outflows of two lakh rupees strictly results in a Net Cash Inflow from Financing Activities equalling four lakh rupees.
